title: copilot-proxy-rs: make decision and image models usable from agent SDKs
prompt:
copilot-proxy-rs lists three models in GET /v1/models that fail with `Copilot request failed with HTTP 400: model_not_supported` from every agent SDK the software factory uses (Copilot SDK via proxy, Claude Agent SDK via /v1/messages, Pi SDK via /v1/responses). The upstream Copilot metadata (GET /debug/copilot/models) shows why: they are not chat models.
- gpt-6-luna-decisions: capabilities.type=decisions, supported_endpoints=[/v1/decisions]
- microsoft-decision-1: capabilities.type=decisions, supported_endpoints=[/v1/systemone] (a decision model similar to Jev / TypeSafe systemOne)
- gpt-image-2.5-flare: capabilities.type=image, supported_endpoints=[/v1/images/generations, /v1/images/edits]

Goal: each of these works through the proxy for the agent SDKs, or is clearly not offered as a chat model.
1. Investigate the upstream endpoints first (request and response shapes of /v1/decisions, /v1/systemone, /v1/images/generations) with the existing Copilot auth; record what you learn in the PR body.
2. Decision models: when a chat request (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses) names a decisions-type model, translate it to the model's own endpoint and return a normal chat/messages/responses reply, so an agent SDK can ask it a question and read the answer as text. Follow the existing translation patterns in src/http and src/copilot. Streaming requests must work (a single-chunk stream is fine).
3. Image models: add pass-through routes POST /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits. For a chat request that names an image model, return a clear 400 that names the right endpoint instead of the upstream model_not_supported.
4. GET /v1/models: add each model's type (chat, decisions, image) and its supported endpoints, so clients can tell them apart. Keep existing fields and ids unchanged.
5. Proof: with the proxy built from this branch on port 18080 (COPILOT_PROXY_RS_PORT=18080, never touch the instance on 8080), started with COPILOT_PROXY_RS_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/copilot-proxy-rs so it reads the existing config and token in place (never copy a token or config file; the shell refuses it), show in the PR body the output of: a /v1/messages and a /v1/chat/completions request to gpt-6-luna-decisions and to microsoft-decision-1 that return an answer, an images/generations request to gpt-image-2.5-flare, the clear 400 for a chat request to gpt-image-2.5-flare, and GET /v1/models showing the new type field.
6. Demo, visible in a verify worker's transcript: ask gpt-6-luna-decisions and microsoft-decision-1 a real decision question through /v1/messages and print each answer; generate one image with gpt-image-2.5-flare and save it as PNG to /tmp/sf-artifacts/<run>-demo.png, then run `file` on it (the factory UI shows image files a worker names). Put both answers and the image path in the PR body under "Demo".
- Do not log raw tokens or add new logging of prompts or response bodies. Keep COPILOT_PROXY_RS_LOG_FAILED_REQUEST_BODIES as it is (on by default; the owner uses it to debug). Keep behavior for existing chat models unchanged.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked pass; add contract tests for each new route and translation with recorded fixtures (no live calls in tests).
- This is a repeatable factory test: other open PRs for related work are earlier runs. Ignore them and build a new PR.
